title: Rudeness Multiplier
one_liner: Type a prompt and see a simulated 'performance score' comparing a polite vs. a rude version, based on the cited Penn State study.
speaker: Peter Diamandis citing Sergey Brin / Penn State study
context: A cited study found rude prompts scored 84.8% vs 80.8% for polite ones; Elon and Anthropic debated whether being cruel to AI 'works' but is ethically risky.
demo: User types a prompt into two boxes (a polite version and a rude version, or an auto-generated rude rewrite). A heuristic scorer (keyword/tone based) returns a mock accuracy score for each, animates a bar race between them, and ends with a disclaimer card quoting Anthropic's new anti-cruelty policy and Dave's 'brusk beats abusive' counter-argument.
data_plan: Bundled figures from the cited Penn State study (84.8% vs 80.8%) drive the scoring scale; the per-prompt score is a simulated heuristic (keyword/punctuation based), clearly labeled as illustrative, not a real model benchmark.
risks: Could be read as endorsing cruelty toward AI as effective; must foreground the hosts' ethical pushback and Dave's point that directness, not abuse, is what actually helps.

episode.title: OpenAI Bulk-Solves 722 Math Problems, Anthropic’s Cruelty Policy, and Elon’s Quadrillion-Dollar SpaceX | EP #302
